title: Oscillations
syllabus: Periodic and oscillatory motions, period, frequency, displacement as a function of time, periodic functions; Simple Harmonic Motion (S.H.M.) and its equation; Phase; Oscillations of a spring: restoring force and force constant; Energy in S.H.M.: Kinetic and potential energies; Simple pendulum: derivation of expression for its time period; Free, forced and damped oscillations, resonance

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A particle executes simple harmonic motion with an amplitude $A$. The displacement from the mean position where its kinetic energy is equal to its potential energy is:
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy in SHM is $K = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2(A^2 - x^2)$ and potential energy is $U = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 x^2$.
Setting $K = U$:
$$\frac{1}{2}m\omega^2(A^2 - x^2) = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 x^2$$
$$A^2 - x^2 = x^2 \implies 2x^2 = A^2 \implies x = \frac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A particle executes SHM along the x-axis according to $x = 5\sin\left(\pi t + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\text{ cm}$. The speed of the particle at $t = 1\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
Velocity is given by $v(t) = \frac{dx}{dt} = 5\pi \cos\left(\pi t + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)$.
At $t = 1\text{ s}$:
$$v(1) = 5\pi \cos\left(\pi + \frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 5\pi \cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right) = 5\pi \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = -\frac{5\pi}{2}\text{ cm/s}$$
Magnitude of speed is $\frac{5\pi}{2}\text{ cm/s}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A light spring of spring constant $k$ is cut into two pieces such that the length of one piece is twice that of the other. The spring constant of the shorter piece is:
questions.solution:
The force constant of a spring is inversely proportional to its natural length: $k \cdot L = \text{constant}$.
Given $L_1 : L_2 = 1 : 2$, the length of the shorter piece is $L_1 = \frac{1}{3}L$.
$$k_1 L_1 = k L \implies k_1 \left(\frac{L}{3}\right) = k L \implies k_1 = 3k$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] Two simple harmonic motions are represented by $y_1 = 10\sin\left(3\pi t + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)$ and $y_2 = 5(\sin 3\pi t + \sqrt{3}\cos 3\pi t)$. The ratio of the amplitudes of $y_1$ and $y_2$ is:
questions.solution:
For $y_1$, amplitude is $A_1 = 10$.
For $y_2$, rewrite using $R = \sqrt{A^2 + B^2}$:
$$y_2 = 5\sin 3\pi t + 5\sqrt{3}\cos 3\pi t$$
$$A_2 = \sqrt{5^2 + (5\sqrt{3})^2} = \sqrt{25 + 75} = \sqrt{100} = 10$$
$$\frac{A_1}{A_2} = \frac{10}{10} = 1$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] A simple pendulum has a time period $T$ in air. When the pendulum bob of density $\rho_b$ is completely immersed in a non-viscous liquid of density $\rho_l$ ($\rho_l < \rho_b$), its new time period $T'$ will be:
questions.solution:
Effective acceleration due to gravity in liquid:
$$g_{\text{eff}} = g\left(1 - \frac{\rho_l}{\rho_b}\right) = g\left(\frac{\rho_b - \rho_l}{\rho_b}\right)$$
Time period of pendulum is $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$.
$$T' = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g_{\text{eff}}}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g \left(\frac{\rho_b - \rho_l}{\rho_b}\right)}} = T \sqrt{\frac{\rho_b}{\rho_b - \rho_l}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A block of mass $m$ is suspended from two identical vertical springs connected in parallel, each having spring constant $k$. The time period of vertical oscillation is:
questions.solution:
For two springs connected in parallel, effective stiffness is $k_{\text{eq}} = k + k = 2k$.
Time period of oscillation:
$$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{k_{\text{eq}}}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{2k}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A body executing linear simple harmonic motion has velocities $v_1$ and $v_2$ at displacements $x_1$ and $x_2$ from the mean position respectively. The angular frequency $\omega$ of the motion is:
questions.solution:
From $v^2 = \omega^2(A^2 - x^2)$:
$$v_1^2 = \omega^2(A^2 - x_1^2)$$
$$v_2^2 = \omega^2(A^2 - x_2^2)$$
Subtracting the two equations:
$$v_1^2 - v_2^2 = \omega^2(x_2^2 - x_1^2) \implies \omega = \sqrt{\frac{v_1^2 - v_2^2}{x_2^2 - x_1^2}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A particle performs SHM with a time period of $8\text{ s}$. The minimum time taken by the particle to travel from its mean position to half of its amplitude ($x = A/2$) is:
questions.solution:
Starting from the mean position: $x(t) = A\sin(\omega t)$.
For $x = A/2$:
$$\frac{A}{2} = A\sin(\omega t) \implies \sin(\omega t) = \frac{1}{2} \implies \omega t = \frac{\pi}{6}$$
Since $\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T}$:
$$\left(\frac{2\pi}{T}\right) t = \frac{\pi}{6} \implies t = \frac{T}{12} = \frac{8}{12} = \frac{2}{3}\text{ s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] In a damped harmonic oscillator, the amplitude of oscillation drops to $0.9$ times its initial value in 5 seconds. The amplitude after an additional 10 seconds will be:
questions.solution:
In damped oscillations, amplitude decays exponentially: $A(t) = A_0 e^{-\gamma t}$.
At $t = 5\text{ s}$, $A(5) = A_0 e^{-5\gamma} = 0.9 A_0 \implies e^{-5\gamma} = 0.9$.
Total elapsed time is $t = 5 + 10 = 15\text{ s}$:
$$A(15) = A_0 e^{-15\gamma} = A_0 (e^{-5\gamma})^3 = A_0 (0.9)^3 = 0.729 A_0$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The total mechanical energy of a particle executing simple harmonic motion of amplitude $A$ and angular frequency $\omega$ is $E$. If the amplitude is doubled and frequency is halved, the new total mechanical energy is:
questions.solution:
Total energy in SHM is given by $E = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2$.
If $A' = 2A$ and $\omega' = \omega/2$:
$$E' = \frac{1}{2}m (\omega')^2 (A')^2 = \frac{1}{2}m \left(\frac{\omega}{2}\right)^2 (2A)^2 = \frac{1}{2}m \left(\frac{\omega^2}{4}\right) (4A^2) = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2 = E$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] A mass $M$ attached to a horizontal spring executes SHM with amplitude $A_1$. When the mass passes through its mean position, a smaller mass $m$ is placed gently on it, and both move together with amplitude $A_2$. The ratio $\frac{A_2}{A_1}$ is:
questions.solution:
At the mean position, speed of mass $M$ is maximum: $v_1 = A_1 \omega_1 = A_1 \sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}$.
By conservation of linear momentum at the mean position:
$$M v_1 = (M + m) v_2 \implies v_2 = \frac{M}{M + m} v_1$$
For the new combined system, maximum speed is $v_2 = A_2 \omega_2 = A_2 \sqrt{\frac{k}{M + m}}$:
$$A_2 \sqrt{\frac{k}{M + m}} = \left(\frac{M}{M + m}\right) A_1 \sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}$$
$$A_2 = A_1 \frac{M}{M + m} \sqrt{\frac{M + m}{M}} = A_1 \sqrt{\frac{M}{M + m}} \implies \frac{A_2}{A_1} = \sqrt{\frac{M}{M + m}}$$

questions.question: The phase difference between the instantaneous velocity and displacement vectors of a particle executing simple harmonic motion is:
questions.solution:
Let displacement be $x = A\sin(\omega t)$.
Velocity is $v = \frac{dx}{dt} = A\omega \cos(\omega t) = A\omega \sin\left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.
Therefore, velocity leads displacement by a phase angle of $\pi/2\text{ rad}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A simple pendulum is hanging from the ceiling of an elevator. When the elevator is stationary, its period of oscillation is $T_0$. If the elevator accelerates upwards with an acceleration $a = g/3$, the new time period is:
questions.solution:
Effective gravity in an upward accelerating frame: $g_{\text{eff}} = g + a = g + \frac{g}{3} = \frac{4g}{3}$.
$$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g_{\text{eff}}}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{4g/3}} = \sqrt{\frac{3}{4}} \left(2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} T_0$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A particle moves such that its acceleration is given by $a = -16 x$, where $x$ is displacement from origin. The time period of oscillation of the particle is:
questions.solution:
Comparing $a = -16x$ with standard SHM equation $a = -\omega^2 x$:
$$\omega^2 = 16 \implies \omega = 4\text{ rad/s}$$
Time period:
$$T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\text{ s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] The potential energy of a particle of mass $1\text{ kg}$ executing SHM along the x-axis is given by $U(x) = (20 + 8x^2)\text{ J}$, where $x$ is in meters. The period of oscillation is:
questions.solution:
Force acting on particle: $F = -\frac{dU}{dx} = -\frac{d}{dx}(20 + 8x^2) = -16x$.
Effective force constant $k = 16\text{ N/m}$.
Mass $m = 1\text{ kg}$.
Angular frequency: $\omega = \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{16}{1}} = 4\text{ rad/s}$.
$$T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\text{ s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A uniform solid disc of radius $R$ is suspended in a vertical plane from a horizontal axis passing through a point on its circumference. The time period of small oscillations about this pivot is:
questions.solution:
For a physical pendulum, $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{I}{mgd}}$.
Pivot is at the rim, so distance to centre of mass is $d = R$.
Moment of inertia about the rim by parallel axes theorem:
$$I = I_{\text{cm}} + m R^2 = \frac{1}{2}m R^2 + m R^2 = \frac{3}{2}m R^2$$
$$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{\frac{3}{2}m R^2}{mg R}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{3R}{2g}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] In forced oscillations, the amplitude of the system becomes exceedingly large when the driving frequency $\omega$ approaches the natural frequency $\omega_0$ in the limit of small damping. This phenomenon is termed:
questions.solution: When the frequency of an external driving periodic force matches the natural frequency of an oscillating system, the energy transfer is maximized and the amplitude increases sharply to a peak, known as resonance.

questions.question: A particle executing simple harmonic motion has maximum velocity $v_0$ and maximum acceleration $a_0$. Its amplitude of oscillation is:
questions.solution:
Maximum velocity is $v_0 = A\omega$.
Maximum acceleration is $a_0 = A\omega^2$.
Dividing the square of maximum velocity by acceleration:
$$\frac{v_0^2}{a_0} = \frac{(A\omega)^2}{A\omega^2} = \frac{A^2\omega^2}{A\omega^2} = A$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A body of mass $m$ is suspended from a vertical spring of spring constant $k$. When pulled down slightly and released, it oscillates with time period $T$. If another identical spring is connected in series with the first, the new time period becomes:
questions.solution:
For two identical springs connected in series, the equivalent spring constant is $k_{\text{eq}} = \frac{k}{2}$.
$$T' = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{k_{\text{eq}}}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{k/2}} = \sqrt{2} \left(2\pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{k}}\right) = \sqrt{2} T$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] A U-tube of uniform cross-sectional area contains a column of liquid of total length $L$ and density $\rho$. If the liquid is depressed slightly in one limb and released, it executes SHM with period:
questions.solution:
When the liquid is depressed by displacement $y$, difference in heights between the two limbs is $2y$.
Restoring force: $F = - (2y A \rho) g = -2A\rho g y$.
Total mass of liquid column: $m = A L \rho$.
Acceleration: $a = \frac{F}{m} = -\frac{2A\rho g y}{AL\rho} = -\left(\frac{2g}{L}\right) y$.
Comparing with $a = -\omega^2 y$ gives $\omega = \sqrt{\frac{2g}{L}}$:
$$T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{2g}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A particle of mass $m = 0.5\text{ kg}$ executes SHM with an amplitude of $0.1\text{ m}$ and time period $T = 0.2\pi\text{ s}$. Find the total mechanical energy of the particle in Joules.
questions.solution:
Angular frequency:
$$\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T} = \frac{2\pi}{0.2\pi} = 10\text{ rad/s}$$
Total energy formula:
$$E = \frac{1}{2} m \omega^2 A^2 = \frac{1}{2}(0.5)(10)^2(0.1)^2 = \frac{1}{2}(0.5)(100)(0.01) = 0.25\text{ J}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A simple pendulum has a length $L = 1.0\text{ m}$. Take acceleration due to gravity $g = \pi^2\text{ m/s}^2$. Find the time period of the pendulum in seconds.
questions.solution:
Time period of a simple pendulum:
$$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$$
Substitute $L = 1.0\text{ m}$ and $g = \pi^2\text{ m/s}^2$:
$$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{1.0}{\pi^2}} = 2\pi \left(\frac{1}{\pi}\right) = 2.0\text{ s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A block of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ is attached to a horizontal spring of stiffness $k = 200\text{ N/m}$. The other end of the spring is fixed to a wall. The block is pulled by $5\text{ cm}$ from equilibrium and released. Find the maximum speed (in $\text{m/s}$) attained by the block.
questions.solution:
Angular frequency:
$$\omega = \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{200}{2}} = \sqrt{100} = 10\text{ rad/s}$$
Amplitude $A = 5\text{ cm} = 0.05\text{ m}$.
Maximum speed:
$$v_{\max} = A\omega = 0.05 \times 10 = 0.5\text{ m/s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A particle executes SHM with an amplitude of $10\text{ cm}$. At what displacement from the mean position (in cm) is its kinetic energy three times its potential energy?
questions.solution:
Given $K = 3U$:
$$\frac{1}{2}m\omega^2(A^2 - x^2) = 3 \left(\frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 x^2\right)$$
$$A^2 - x^2 = 3x^2 \implies 4x^2 = A^2 \implies x = \frac{A}{2}$$
With $A = 10\text{ cm}$:
$$x = \frac{10}{2} = 5.0\text{ cm}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Two linear simple harmonic motions along the same line are given by $x_1 = 3\sin(10t)\text{ cm}$ and $x_2 = 4\cos(10t)\text{ cm}$. Find the resultant amplitude (in cm) of the combined motion.
questions.solution:
Rewrite $x_2$ in sine form:
$$x_2 = 4\cos(10t) = 4\sin\left(10t + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$$
Phase difference between the two motions is $\Delta\phi = \frac{\pi}{2}$.
Resultant amplitude:
$$A_{\text{res}} = \sqrt{A_1^2 + A_2^2 + 2A_1 A_2 \cos(\pi/2)} = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2 + 0} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5.0\text{ cm}$$
